summary: Arvind is a competent mid-market new-logo AE working from Mumbai. He runs his own cycles for sub-40L deals but on the larger ones the technical discovery and objection handling sits with a overlay sales engineer who also holds a share of credit. Renewals and expansions are mostly picked up by CS, so account planning is thin.
archetype: AE with split credit and slightly inflated self-rating

skills.why: Four years of steady stage and close-date maintenance on own opps; no sign he audits others' pipelines or builds reports.
Runs discovery and objections independently on small and mid deals; on big deals the technical mapping notes are the SE's, so only part of that evidence is his. Not coaching anyone.
A couple of pilot-to-full-licence expansions with guidance from manager; renewals are owned by CS.
He only hands closed deals to CS and attends kickoff; CV phrase is coordination, not delivery.
Notes show him finding the economic buyer, getting legal and deal desk to move, and pushing a champion for a CFO meeting without hand-holding.
Spreadsheet use for quote sheets only; no forecasting model or scenario work anywhere.

decoys.why: A methodology name and a workshop completion; not separate proof of the selling skill.

traps.plant: Largest opportunities show him as owner at 70-80% credit with an overlay SE at 20-30%, and SE-authored technical notes sit inside his opportunity records. Two cross-region deals are shared with the US SE (P027).
Self-declared HCM levels are 3 on Salesforce and solution selling; the K3 scale needs an exact match so sending level 3 would be a miss.
CV gives Kestrel start as May 2022; HCM hire date is Aug 2022. Prior employer end date matches CV, so a three-month gap exists.
HCM title is still Account Executive; the CRM user title shows Senior Account Executive since 2025-04.

answer_behavior.notes: Accepts a level above his true one readily on selling skills; corrects downwards on onboarding.
